---
applyTo: "app/services/**/*.rb,app/forms/**/*.rb,app/controllers/**/*.rb,app/jobs/**/*.rb"
---

# Services

- Put service objects in `app/services/`, e.g. `NewsletterClient` in `app/services/newsletter_client.rb`.
- Never give a service object a `call` method. Name each public method after what it does, e.g. `NewsletterClient#create_newsletter` and `NewsletterClient#deliver`.
- Call a service from an action, never from a form or controller, e.g. `NewsletterClient.new.create_newsletter(post)` in `Posts::SendNewsletter#call`. Forms, controllers and jobs call the action. A form or controller may call a service directly only to read a value when nothing changes, e.g. `NewsletterClient.new.fetch_stats(post.newsletter_id)` in a controller. A job may call a service directly only when it is the only place that does the task, e.g. `NewsletterClient.new.deliver(post)` in `NotifySubscribersJob`. Move the call into an action when a second caller needs it.
- Read a service's settings from a `Rails.application.config.x` namespace named after the service, e.g. `config.x.newsletter_client.api_key`. Set the values in one place, e.g. `config/application.rb`, from credentials or `ENV`. Never read `Rails.application.credentials` or `ENV` in a service, and never put a setting straight on `config.x`, e.g. `config.x.newsletter_client_api_key`.
- Take each setting as a keyword argument to `initialize`, with the setting as its default, e.g. `def initialize(api_key: Rails.application.config.x.newsletter_client.api_key!)`. Read required settings with a bang, e.g. `api_key!`, so a missing or blank value raises a `KeyError`. Never pass the settings from app code, e.g. `NewsletterClient.new`, not `NewsletterClient.new(api_key: ...)`. Only specs pass them, e.g. `described_class.new(api_key: "test-key")`.
- When a service's settings are saved on a record, build it with a class method on the service that passes the record's settings to `new`, named `for` or `for_<source>`, e.g. `for_integration`. For example, `def self.for(integration) = new(api_key: integration.api_key, base_url: integration.base_url)` on `NewsletterClient`. Make those settings required keywords with no default, and leave app-wide settings to their `config.x` defaults, e.g. `api_path: Rails.application.config.x.newsletter_client.api_path!`. Never add a method to the record that builds the service, e.g. `integration.client`.
- When a service keeps connections open to another service, borrow them from a `ConnectionPool` kept on the service in a private `Concurrent::Map` constant and keyed on the connection settings, e.g. `POOLS.compute_if_absent({ base_url: })` in `NewsletterClient.pool_for(base_url:)`. Take the pool as a required first argument to `initialize`, e.g. `def initialize(pool, api_key:)`, and borrow from it in each method, e.g. `pool.with { |connection| ... }`. Build the service with a class method that finds the pool: `NewsletterClient.default` when every setting comes from `config.x`, e.g. `new(pool_for(base_url: Rails.application.config.x.newsletter_client.base_url!), api_key: Rails.application.config.x.newsletter_client.api_key!)`, or `NewsletterClient.for(integration)` (or `for_integration`) when the settings come from a record, e.g. `new(pool_for(base_url: integration.base_url), api_key: integration.api_key)`. Pass connection settings only to `pool_for`, and keep `pool_for` private. Never pass a pool to `new` from outside the service. Only specs and the service's own class methods pass one. Never let a pooled connection carry one set of credentials to a service built with another. Send credentials with each request, e.g. an `Authorization` header, or include them in the pool's key. See https://bmorrall.github.io/happy_rails/patterns/connection-pools/.
- TODO: Which kinds of service objects to write.
- Give each service its own errors: an `Error < StandardError` class inside the service, and a subclass for each failure a caller handles on its own, e.g. `NewsletterClient::UnprocessableError < Error`. Rescue the HTTP library's errors in the service and raise the service's error, e.g. `rescue Faraday::Error => e` then `raise Error.new(e.message, ...)`. Never let a library's error escape a service.
- Give a service's error the details of the failed call as keywords, e.g. `http_method:`, `url:`, `status:` and `body:` on `NewsletterClient::Error`.
